```{r setup, include=FALSE}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Manuscript tables (Word output)
#
# Builds the formatted tables for the manuscript from the CSV files written by
# climate_analysis.R. Run climate_analysis.R FIRST, then knit this file
# (RStudio: "Knit" button, or rmarkdown::render("manuscript_tables.Rmd")).
#
#   Table 1    Climate quartile by gender x racial identification x institution type
#   Table 2    Standardized chi-square residuals for the same grouping
#   Table 3    Three-way ART ANOVA
#   Table A1   Factor loadings and item weights (3-factor EFA)
#   Table A2   Item means by climate quartile
#
# Every sample size, fit statistic and cut point quoted in a table footnote is
# read from the analysis output -- nothing is hardcoded here.
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(flextable)
library(officer)

# Folder written by climate_analysis.R
data_dir <- "output"

set_flextable_defaults(
  font.family  = "Times New Roman",
  font.size    = 9,
  table.layout = "autofit",
  border.color = "black"
)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Helpers
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Read a CSV from data_dir; return NULL (with a message) if it is missing
read_csv_safe <- function(filename) {
  path <- file.path(data_dir, filename)
  if (!file.exists(path)) {
    message("File not found: ", path, " -- skipping")
    return(NULL)
  }
  read.csv(path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE, check.names = FALSE)
}

# Sample sizes
n_tab <- read_csv_safe("Sample_sizes.csv")
if (is.null(n_tab))
  stop("Sample_sizes.csv not found in '", data_dir, "'. Run climate_analysis.R first.")
get_n <- function(key) {
  v <- n_tab$n[n_tab$sample == key]
  if (length(v) != 1) stop("Sample size '", key, "' not found in Sample_sizes.csv")
  v
}
fmt_n   <- function(x) format(x, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE)
n_cit   <- get_n("citizens_PR")        # U.S. citizens / permanent residents
n_chisq <- get_n("who_exp_analytic")   # gender x race x institution analyses
n_art   <- get_n("art_2x2x2")          # three-way ART ANOVA sample
n_q     <- unname(sapply(paste0("quartile_Q", 1:4), get_n))   # Q1-Q4 counts

# Other statistics quoted in footnotes (fit indices, quartile cut points)
stat_tab <- read_csv_safe("Key_statistics.csv")
if (is.null(stat_tab))
  stop("Key_statistics.csv not found in '", data_dir, "'. Run climate_analysis.R first.")
get_stat <- function(key) {
  v <- stat_tab$value[stat_tab$statistic == key]
  if (length(v) != 1) stop("Statistic '", key, "' not found in Key_statistics.csv")
  v
}

# Format p-values for display
fmt_p <- function(p) {
  ifelse(p < .001, "< .001", formatC(p, digits = 3, format = "f"))
}

# Generic flextable builder: rounds numeric columns, adds a bold caption and
# italic footnotes
make_ft <- function(df, title, footnotes = NULL, digits = 2,
                    col_labels = NULL, bold_col = NULL) {

  num_cols <- which(sapply(df, is.numeric))
  df[num_cols] <- lapply(df[num_cols], round, digits = digits)

  ft <- flextable(df)

  if (!is.null(col_labels))
    ft <- set_header_labels(ft, values = col_labels)

  ft <- ft |>
    bold(part = "header") |>
    align(align = "left",   part = "body") |>
    align(j = num_cols, align = "right", part = "body") |>
    align(part = "header", align = "center") |>
    fontsize(size = 9, part = "all") |>
    padding(padding = 2, part = "all") |>
    set_caption(
      caption = as_paragraph(as_b(title)),
      fp_p    = fp_par(text.align = "left", padding.bottom = 4)
    ) |>
    autofit()

  if (!is.null(bold_col))
    ft <- bold(ft, j = bold_col, part = "body")

  if (!is.null(footnotes)) {
    for (fn in footnotes)
      ft <- add_footer_lines(ft, values = fn)
    ft <- fontsize(ft, size = 8, part = "footer") |>
          italic(part = "footer")
  }
  ft
}
```

```{r table1-descriptive}
# Table 1: distribution of climate quartile by gender x racial identification,
# shown as two panels (PWI and HBCU). All three levels of gender and racial
# identification are kept, including "Prefer not to say/Other". Inference is
# carried by the ART ANOVA (Table 3), not by this table.
#
# Racial-identification labels: WA = White and/or Asian, BHI = Black, Hispanic,
# and/or Indigenous (the "NotURM" / "URM" values in the data).
df_raw <- read_csv_safe("Table1_quartile_by_gender_race_insttype.csv")
if (!is.null(df_raw)) {

  gender_levels <- c("Female", "Male", "Prefer not to say/Other")
  urm_levels    <- c("WA", "BHI", "Prefer not to say/Other")

  # Reshape to one row per Gender x URM x institution, one column per quartile
  df_wide <- df_raw |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      Gender = factor(Gender, levels = gender_levels),
      URM    = factor(dplyr::recode(URM, "NotURM" = "WA", "URM" = "BHI"),
                      levels = urm_levels)
    ) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = ClimateQuartile, values_from = Freq, values_fill = 0) |>
    dplyr::arrange(UnivType, URM, Gender) |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      Total = Q1 + Q2 + Q3 + Q4,
      # Cell text "count (row %)", e.g. "91 (36%)"; guard against empty rows
      Q1_disp = ifelse(Total > 0, sprintf("%d (%.0f%%)", Q1, 100 * Q1 / Total), "0"),
      Q2_disp = ifelse(Total > 0, sprintf("%d (%.0f%%)", Q2, 100 * Q2 / Total), "0"),
      Q3_disp = ifelse(Total > 0, sprintf("%d (%.0f%%)", Q3, 100 * Q3 / Total), "0"),
      Q4_disp = ifelse(Total > 0, sprintf("%d (%.0f%%)", Q4, 100 * Q4 / Total), "0")
    )

  make_panel <- function(univ) {
    df_wide |>
      dplyr::filter(UnivType == univ) |>
      dplyr::select(Gender, URM, n = Total, Q1 = Q1_disp, Q2 = Q2_disp,
                    Q3 = Q3_disp, Q4 = Q4_disp)
  }

  # One shaded header row per institution type, then that panel's rows
  panel_header <- function(label) {
    data.frame(Gender = label, URM = "", n = NA_integer_,
               Q1 = "", Q2 = "", Q3 = "", Q4 = "", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  }
  display <- bind_rows(panel_header("PWI"),  make_panel("PWI"),
                       panel_header("HBCU"), make_panel("HBCU"))

  # N actually shown in the table, taken from the data. If it is smaller than
  # the full sample, say so in the footnote rather than overstating N.
  table_n <- sum(df_wide$Total)
  n_gap   <- n_cit - table_n
  n_note  <- if (n_gap > 0) {
    paste0(" Note: this table includes ", table_n, " of ", fmt_n(n_cit),
           " citizen/permanent-resident respondents; ", n_gap,
           " respondent(s) had missing institution type, gender, or racial",
           " identification data and are not represented in any row above.")
  } else {
    ""
  }

  ft <- flextable(display) |>
    set_header_labels(
      values = list(
        Gender = "Group", URM = "Racial Identification", n = "n",
        Q1 = "Q1", Q2 = "Q2", Q3 = "Q3", Q4 = "Q4"
      )
    ) |>
    bold(part = "header") |>
    align(part = "header", align = "center") |>
    align(j = c("n", "Q1", "Q2", "Q3", "Q4"), align = "right", part = "body") |>
    fontsize(size = 9, part = "all") |>
    padding(padding = 2, part = "all") |>
    # Bold + shade the PWI / HBCU header rows
    bold(i = which(display$URM == ""), part = "body") |>
    bg(i = which(display$URM == ""), bg = "#F0F0F0", part = "body") |>
    set_caption(
      caption = as_paragraph(as_b(
        paste0(
          "Table 1. Distribution of composite climate score quartile by gender, ",
          "Racial Identification, and institution type for U.S. citizen/permanent-resident ",
          "respondents."
        )
      )),
      fp_p = fp_par(text.align = "left", padding.bottom = 4)
    ) |>
    add_footer_lines(paste0(
      "*N = ", fmt_n(table_n), ". Cell values are n (% of row total).", n_note
    )) |>
    fontsize(size = 8, part = "footer") |>
    italic(part = "footer") |>
    autofit()

  ft
}
```

```{r table2-stdres}
# Table 2: standardized residuals from the chi-square test of the
# gender x racial identification x institution-type grouping vs. climate quartile.
#
# The CSV has an unnamed first column holding row labels such as
# "Female_NotURM_PWI". Gender and URM labels can contain spaces and slashes but
# never underscores, so the label is split by stripping the known institution
# and URM suffixes from right to left rather than by splitting on "_".
# Residuals with |z| > 2 are shown in bold.
df_res <- read_csv_safe("Table2_standardized_residuals.csv")
if (!is.null(df_res)) {

  names(df_res)[1] <- "group_combo"

  inst_vals <- c("PWI", "HBCU")
  urm_vals  <- c("NotURM", "URM", "Prefer not to say/Other")

  parse_combo <- function(x) {
    inst <- inst_vals[sapply(inst_vals, function(i) endsWith(x, paste0("_", i)))]
    rest <- substr(x, 1, nchar(x) - nchar(inst) - 1L)
    urm  <- urm_vals[sapply(urm_vals, function(u) endsWith(rest, paste0("_", u)))]
    gndr <- substr(rest, 1, nchar(rest) - nchar(urm) - 1L)
    c(gndr, urm, inst)
  }

  parsed <- t(sapply(df_res$group_combo, parse_combo))
  df_res$Gender       <- parsed[, 1]
  df_res$`URM Status` <- parsed[, 2]
  df_res$Institution  <- parsed[, 3]

  # Display labels (WA = White and/or Asian; BHI = Black, Hispanic, Indigenous)
  df_res$`URM Status` <- dplyr::recode(df_res$`URM Status`,
    "NotURM" = "WA",
    "URM"    = "BHI",
    "Prefer not to say/Other" = "Prefer not to say/Other"
  )

  # Row order: PWI then HBCU; within each, URM status then gender
  gender_ord <- c("Female", "Male", "Prefer not to say/Other")
  urm_ord    <- c("WA", "BHI", "Prefer not to say/Other")
  inst_ord   <- c("PWI", "HBCU")

  df_res <- df_res |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      Gender       = factor(Gender,        levels = gender_ord),
      `URM Status` = factor(`URM Status`,  levels = urm_ord),
      Institution  = factor(Institution,   levels = inst_ord)
    ) |>
    dplyr::arrange(Institution, `URM Status`, Gender) |>
    dplyr::select(Institution, Gender, `URM Status`, Q1, Q2, Q3, Q4)

  ft_res <- flextable(df_res) |>
    set_header_labels(values = list(
      Institution  = "Institution",
      Gender       = "Gender",
      `URM Status` = "Racial Identification",
      Q1 = "Q1", Q2 = "Q2", Q3 = "Q3", Q4 = "Q4"
    )) |>
    bold(part = "header") |>
    align(part = "header", align = "center") |>
    align(j = c("Q1", "Q2", "Q3", "Q4"), align = "right", part = "body") |>
    fontsize(size = 9, part = "all") |>
    padding(padding = 2, part = "all") |>
    set_caption(
      caption = as_paragraph(as_b(
        paste0(
          "Table 2: Standardized chi-square residuals: Gender x Racial Identification x ",
          "Institution Type vs. climate score quartile."
        )
      )),
      fp_p = fp_par(text.align = "left", padding.bottom = 4)
    )

  # Bold residuals beyond |2|, the conventional threshold for a meaningful
  # departure from independence
  for (qcol in c("Q1", "Q2", "Q3", "Q4")) {
    rows_bold <- which(abs(df_res[[qcol]]) > 2)
    if (length(rows_bold) > 0)
      ft_res <- bold(ft_res, i = rows_bold, j = qcol, part = "body")
  }

  # Light shading for HBCU rows
  hbcu_rows <- which(df_res$Institution == "HBCU")
  if (length(hbcu_rows) > 0)
    ft_res <- bg(ft_res, i = hbcu_rows, bg = "#F7F7F7", part = "body")

  ft_res <- ft_res |>
    add_footer_lines(paste0(
      "*N = ", fmt_n(n_chisq), ". Standardized residuals (z) reported from chi-square test of independence ",
      "between the Gender x Racial Identification x Institution Type and climate score ",
      "quartile. Due to sparse HBCU combinations, > 20% of expected cell counts ",
      "were < 5 and Monte Carlo chi-square p value (B = 10,000) was used for ",
      "inference rather than the asymptotic distribution. Standardized residuals ",
      "from this test are reported with bolded values indicating |z| > 2.00, ",
      "a meaningful departure from the expected frequency under independence. ",
      "Positive values indicate the group is overrepresented in that quartile ",
      "relative to expectation; negative values indicate underrepresentation."
    )) |>
    fontsize(size = 8, part = "footer") |>
    italic(part = "footer") |>
    autofit()

  ft_res
}
```

```{r table3-art}
# Table 3: three-way ART ANOVA (racial identification x gender x institution type)
df <- read_csv_safe("Table3_ART_anova.csv")
if (!is.null(df)) {

  # write.csv() adds a row-label column; drop it
  if (names(df)[1] %in% c("", "X", "V1") || grepl("^[0-9]", names(df)[1]))
    df <- df[, -1]

  # Human-readable effect names. In the analysis code the factors are called
  # urm3 / gender3 / univ_type; the "3" is a leftover from the three-level
  # coding they started from. In this ANOVA each factor has exactly TWO levels
  # (Male/Female, URM/NotURM, PWI/HBCU), so every effect has 1 numerator df.
  term_map <- c(
    "urm3"                   = "Racial Identification",
    "gender3"                = "Gender",
    "univ_type"              = "Institution Type (PWI vs. HBCU)",
    "urm3:gender3"           = "Racial Identification x Gender",
    "urm3:univ_type"         = "Racial Identification x Institution Type",
    "gender3:univ_type"      = "Gender x Institution Type",
    "urm3:gender3:univ_type" = "Racial Identification x Gender x Institution Type"
  )

  names(df)[1] <- "Effect"
  df$Effect <- ifelse(df$Effect %in% names(term_map),
                      term_map[df$Effect], df$Effect)

  # Format the p-value column
  p_col <- grep("Pr|p.value|p_value", names(df), value = TRUE)[1]
  df[[p_col]] <- fmt_p(df[[p_col]])

  df_disp <- dplyr::select(df,
    Effect,
    Df    = dplyr::matches("^Df$"),
    DfRes = dplyr::matches("Df.res"),
    F     = dplyr::matches("F.value|F value"),
    p     = dplyr::all_of(p_col)
  )

  ft3 <- make_ft(
    df_disp,
    title = paste0(
      "Table 3: Three-way Aligned Rank Transform (ART) ANOVA: effects of ",
      "Racial Identification, gender, and institution type on composite climate score."
    ),
    digits = 3,
    col_labels = list(
      Effect = "Effect",
      Df     = "df",
      DfRes  = "df (residual)",
      F      = "F",
      p      = "p"
    ),
    footnotes = c(
      paste0(
        "*N = ", fmt_n(n_art), ". Sample restricted to Female/Male respondents with BHI/WA status ",
        "(", fmt_n(n_art), " of ", fmt_n(n_cit), " citizens/PRs; ", fmt_n(n_cit - n_art),
        " excluded due to 'Prefer not to say/Other' responses in gender or racial identification, ",
        "which created empty cells in the HBCU x Prefer-not-to-say combinations, ",
        "precluding full factorial estimation)."
      )
    )
  )

  # Extra left padding and a thin border on the p column so it reads as
  # visually separate from F
  ft3 <- ft3 |>
    padding(j = "p", padding.left = 14, part = "all") |>
    border(j = "p", border.left = fp_border(color = "#CCCCCC", width = 1),
           part = "all")

  ft3
}
```

```{r tableA1-loadings}
# Appendix Table A1: factor loadings and item weights (citizens-only 3-factor EFA).
# Factor columns are already ordered by content in climate_analysis.R:
#   Factor 1 = departmental/relational climate, Factor 2 = advisor relationship,
#   Factor 3 = research/professional engagement.
df <- read_csv_safe("TableA1_citizens_EFA_loadings.csv")
if (!is.null(df)) {

  df <- dplyr::select(df, Item, Factor1, Factor2, Factor3, PrimaryFactor, WeightUsed)

  # Items whose largest loading was below 0.30 were given weight 0; name them
  zero_items <- df$Item[df$WeightUsed == 0]
  zero_note <- if (length(zero_items) == 0) {
    ""
  } else {
    paste0(
      if (length(zero_items) == 1) "One item (" else paste0(length(zero_items), " items ("),
      paste0("'", zero_items, "'", collapse = ", "),
      ") with no loading >= |0.30| on any factor received weight = 0. "
    )
  }

  make_ft(
    df,
    title  = paste0(
      "Table A1: Factor loadings and item weights from the three-factor ",
      "exploratory factor analysis of climate survey items ",
      "(U.S. citizen/permanent-resident respondents)"
    ),
    digits = 2,
    col_labels = list(
      Item          = "Survey Item",
      Factor1       = "Factor 1\n(Dept./Relational Climate)",
      Factor2       = "Factor 2\n(Advisor Relationship)",
      Factor3       = "Factor 3\n(Research/Professional Engagement)",
      PrimaryFactor = "Primary Factor",
      WeightUsed    = "Item Weight"
    ),
    footnotes = c(
      paste0(
        "*N = ", fmt_n(n_cit), ". Oblique (oblimin) rotation; polychoric correlations. ",
        "Primary Factor = factor on which item loaded most strongly (|loading|); ",
        "Item Weight = that loading, used to construct the composite climate score. ",
        zero_note,
        "RMSEA = ", sprintf("%.3f", get_stat("efa_cit3_RMSEA")),
        ", TLI = ",  sprintf("%.3f", get_stat("efa_cit3_TLI")),
        " for the three-factor solution."
      )
    )
  )
}
```

```{r tableA2-quartile-means}
# Appendix Table A2: mean item response by climate-score quartile
df <- read_csv_safe("TableA2_item_means_by_quartile.csv")
if (!is.null(df)) {
  cuts <- sprintf("%.2f", c(get_stat("quartile_cut_25"),
                            get_stat("quartile_cut_50"),
                            get_stat("quartile_cut_75")))
  make_ft(
    df,
    title  = paste0(
      "Table A2: Mean survey item response by composite climate score quartile ",
      "(U.S. citizen/permanent-resident respondents)"
    ),
    digits = 2,
    col_labels = list(Item = "Survey Item", Q1 = "Q1", Q2 = "Q2", Q3 = "Q3", Q4 = "Q4"),
    footnotes = c(
      paste0(
        "*N = ", fmt_n(n_cit), ". Items are rescaled to a 1-4 metric (five-point items linearly ",
        "rescaled; see Methods). Quartile cut points: ", paste(cuts, collapse = " / "), ". ",
        "Quartile n: Q1 = ", n_q[1], ", Q2 = ", n_q[2], ", Q3 = ", n_q[3],
        ", Q4 = ", n_q[4], "."
      )
    )
  )
}
```
